data.name: Bijendra
data.gender_notes: Bijendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bijendra is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Bija' (seed) and 'Indra' (god of thunder). The name means 'Conqueror of Bijas'. In Hindu mythology, Indra is the king of heaven and the god of rain, thunder, and lightning. The name Bijendra is believed to bring victory and success. The name Bijendra carries the meaning “Conqueror of Bijas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bijendra usually hope their child will grow to embody conqueror of bijas and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bijendra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Conqueror of Bijas.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bijendra total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Bijendra is a name that speaks of power, courage, and dominion. It is a name that resonates with the strength and might of Indra, the Hindu god of rain, thunder, and lightning. In Indian culture, there is a deep reverence for the gods and goddesses, and naming a child after a deity is believed to bestow Upon the child the blessings and protection of that deity. Thus, the name Bijendra signifies the divine blessing and support of Indra, the deity of power and might.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Bijendra represents the inner power and strength that lies within each one of us. Just like Indra, who wielded the power of the thunderbolt, we too have the power to conquer our thoughts, our fears, and our limitations. The name is a reminder that we are all powerful beings, capable of overcoming obstacles and achieving great things. It is a call to tap into our inner strength and courage, and to use it to fulfill our potential and make a positive impact in the world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Bijendra was a king in the Gupta Empire during the 5th century AD. The name Bijendra carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Bijendra remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Devi Bijendra in Kathmandu, Nepal attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Bijendra, which means "Conqueror of Bijas". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
